title: Limited Competition Justification and Award Notice - Upgrade of Simplex System and FM-200 Systems
description: The purpose of this notice is to comply with the public posting requirements of FAR Part 5 and FAR 6.103-1. The requirement is for the upgrade, modification, and enhancement of the existing installed Simplex Fire Alarm and FM-200 Systems at the USAGM Kuwait Transmitting Station. The scope of work includes the supply of genuine manufacturer approved Simplex components, installation, proprietary system programming, software configuration, testing, commissioning, and integration with the existing system. This acquisition is being conducted under FAR Part 12. Competition was limited because only one responsible source is reasonably available to satisfy the Government's minimum requirements. Interests span the software lifecycle and include: a.Low-code and no-code development platforms and services b.Integration services c.Automated continuous delivery capabilities d.Platform observability and health monitoring solutions e.Operational analytics f.Baseline configuration management g.Automated incident response h.Resilient platform operations i.Solutions should reduce Government integration complexity, shorten the time to fieldsoftware to operations, and lower the compliance and management burden on the Government, while enabling a scalable, modular, and interoperable software ecosystem 3.FAS #2 (AOI 04-FAS02): The Kronos FoS seeks innovative commercial products and services that automate execution of the Risk Management Framework (RMF) and radicallycompress the time required to achieve and maintain authorization across the Kronos Family ofSystems. Interests span all six RMF steps. Solutions may employ artificial intelligence, machinelearning, or other automation, and include: a.System categorization and security control selection b.Control implementation and configuration enforcement c.Continuous control assessment and automated evidence collection d.Security documentation, Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) management, and authorization package generation e.Continuous monitoring, and real-time risk posture visibility f.Security impact analysis and change request disposition g.Vulnerability management, incident detection, automated response, and recovery h.Software assurance and cyber analytics supporting operational resiliency i.Solutions should reduce the time to achieve and maintain an authorization to operate,eliminate manual and duplicative compliance effort, and give the Government continuous, evidence-based visibility of its cybersecurity risk posture 4.Submission Timeline: Questions regarding this Call shall be submitted no later than 1200 Pacific Time on 07 August 2026. Responses to submitted questions will be posted to SAM.gov(http://sam.gov). Phase 1A submissions (Quad Chart and White Paper) shall be received no later than 1700 Pacific Time on 26 August 2026. 5.Additional Information: All submission instructions, eligibility requirements, evaluationprocedures, and applicable terms and conditions are contained within the Kronos FoS CSO.Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov (http://sam.gov) for amendments, answers toquestions, and any updates associated with this Call. title: Y--Synopsis - Construct North Unit Visitor Center
description: PURPOSE: This notice is a synopsis of an upcoming Construction requirement at Badlands National Park; this is NOT a formal solicitation. SYNOPSIS OF WORK: The National Park Service has a requirement to construct a NEW visitor center on the south side of Badlands Loop Road located between the old Ben Reifel Visitor Center and the Cedar Pass Lodge. Large, north-facing windows will immerse visitors in the badlands landscape. The project will allow for expansion due to increased yearly visitation and will provide a more positive visitor experience. This is being constructed following an overall revamp review of the developed area. Construction of one new facility (new VC) allows other existing facilities to be repurposed; this approach will maximize those facilities which can be saved and will endure into the years. NAICS: The affiliated NAICS for this effort will be 236220 with a Small Business Size Standard of $45M. Alternative NAICS may be considered by the CO, however, firms wishing to participate in the upcoming solicitation should register under the NAICS to be considered for award. SET ASIDES: The NPS will likely set this requirement aside for 100% Small Businesses. MAGNITUDE: The EMC is $10 to $20M WAGE DETERMINATIONS: A Davis Bacon Wage Determination will apply for the county in which work will commence. ESTIMATED SOLICITATION DATE: 9/3/2026. SITE VISIT: A virtual site visit (going over Specs & Drawings) will take place as prescribed in the solicitation, when released. Contractors will be encouraged to visit the site at their own discretion, as it is open to the public for viewing. SELECTION METHOD: FAR 14 Sealed Bidding. The solicitation will likely be in the form of an Invitation for Bid. Selection will be made to the bidder who submits the lowest price and is considered to be Responsible. SOLICITATION ATTACHMENTS: Attachments will include all relevant data necessary for contractors to formulate accurate/reliable bids. These may include Specifications, Drawings, Reports, Maps, Studies, etc. Attachments are NOT present in this Synopsis but will be readily available on the SAM.Gov solicitation announcement, likely to be posted the first week of September. RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE ARE NOT REQUIRED: Responses to this notice are not required or desired. Please be on the lookout for the formal solicitation around the first week of September. CONTRACTING POC: Cole Johnson, Contracting Officer, DOI - National Park Service, Cole_Johnson@NPS.Gov

title: Q601--Medical Coding Auditing
description: The VA Greater Los Angeles Health Care System had an urgent requirement for medical coding and auditing services. This was an urgent requirement to ensure the timely and accurate processing of healthcare documentation and billing to prevent disruptions to veteran care. A three-month contract was urgently required to ensure uninterrupted service delivery while allowing sufficient time for the proper procurement and competition of a new long-term contract. Cooper Thomas was the only vendor able to meet this requirement because they are the incumbent contractor with an already-approved FITARA. Engaging a new vendor would necessitate a separate FITARA approval and a full onboarding process, both of which would introduce significant delays and risk to mission continuity.
